author: Jan Kampherbeek

methods.construction: Trisect ecliptic arcs between ASC, IC, DSC and MC.
Solve ecliptic points whose right ascension offsets equal one-third/two-thirds of their semi-diurnal or semi-nocturnal arcs.
Trisect celestial-equator quadrants; project via great circles through the north/south horizon axis.
Trisect prime-vertical quadrants; project via great circles through the north/south horizon axis.

implementation: Original vector geometry and semi-arc root solver; Swiss only supplies test references.
assignment: Half-open ecliptic-longitude sectors, not latitude-aware mundane placement.
polar_policy: All quadrant methods explicitly reject abs(latitude) >= 90 - true obliquity. Placidus semi-arcs become circumpolar; other methods may be defined but polar orientation is outside this release's validated domain. No fallback.
interpretation: A house-system choice changes geometric placements. It does not establish that a reading has greater predictive validity. System-specific interpretive rules are not treated as interchangeable.
rights: Mathematical constructions summarized; no source code or book text copied.
